title: oneway
text: core function package pairwise_comparison(), provides ---box statistical inference one-way designs. expects data frame two-sided formula: function return list includes 5 components: method: combination priori post-hoc test; data: input data; pre_hoc: ANOVA-like table selected priori test; post_hoc: pairwise comparison result selected post hoc test; summary: descriptive statistics reporting. post_hoc component data frame least 15 columns: summary component data frame 13 columns:

title: oneway
text: classic ANOVA procedure parametric analysis oneway_anova(). function checks normality variance homogeneity. var_equal = NA (default), uses varequal::is_var_equal check variance homogeneity decide conduct: Fisher’s one-way ANOVA equal variances supported; Welch’s ANOVA equal variances supported. can also force procedure: Reading ANOVA table Fisher/Welch’s ANOVA output includes columns : DF: degrees freedom; SS: sum squares; MS: mean square; Fvalue: observed F statistic; Fcrit: critical F value; Pvalue: omnibus p-value; signif: significance label; p_omega2: partial omega-squared effect size; method: Fisher’s Welch’s ANOVA. automatic selection convenient exploratory routine analyses, still important examine study design diagnostics interpreting result.
code: anova_ooo <- oneway_anova(O_O_O, val ~ grp) anova_ooo #>            DF       SS      MS  Fvalue  Fcrit Pvalue signif p_omega2 #> Group       5 160.7404 32.1481 41.2416 2.2939      0    ***   0.6264 #> Residuals 114  88.8637  0.7795      NA     NA     NA   <NA>       NA #> Total     119 249.6041      NA      NA     NA     NA   <NA>       NA #>                   method #> Group     Fisher's ANOVA #> Residuals Fisher's ANOVA #> Total     Fisher's ANOVA fisher <- oneway_anova(O_O_O, val ~ grp, var_equal = TRUE) welch <- oneway_anova(O_X_X, val ~ grp, var_equal = FALSE)

title: oneway
text: oneway implements five multiple comparison procedures (MCPs) post hoc analysis. procedure returns results standardized format consistent pairwise_comparison(). Although MCPs can applied directly without priori adjustment protection, interpretation nevertheless informed outcome omnibus test. particular, evidence omnibus test provides overall assessment whether differences among group means warrant subsequent pairwise comparisons.

title: oneway
text: pairwise_comparison() automatically implements conventional workflow one-way analysis evaluating relevant distributional variance assumptions, selecting appropriate omnibus test, subsequently performing pairwise comparisons warranted. decision logic : adaptive workflow can therefore return 7 complete protocols: one-way ANOVA + REGWQ; one-way ANOVA + Tukey–Kramer; one-way ANOVA + Games–Howell; ART-ANOVA + [REGWQ y’’]; ART-ANOVA + [Tukey–Kramer y’’]; ART-ANOVA + [Games–Howell y’’]; Kruskal–Wallis + Dunn. Fisher’s Welch’s ANOVA procedures conducted residuals rather raw response.

title: oneway
text: compact letter display presentation device: groups sharing letter significantly different; groups without common letter significantly different. compact_letter_display() can used independently. example: centers argument controls order used assign letters. parametric procedures typically natural use mean; rank-based procedures, median appropriate. symbols can also customized: two-samples comparison, use pval2asterisk() convert numeric p-values user-defined significance symbols. default labels : Custom thresholds symbols supported. function expects thresholds descending order:
code: dunn <- Dunn_test(X_X_O, val ~ grp, verbose = FALSE)  summary_tab <- row_arrange(dunn$summary, cols = "MED")  padj_name <- "Padj (holm)"  cld <- compact_letter_display(x1 = dunn$post_hoc$x1,                               x2 = dunn$post_hoc$x2,                               pvalues = dunn$post_hoc[[padj_name]],                               grp_names = summary_tab$GROUP,                               centers = summary_tab$MED)  cld #>   G3   G6   G2   G5   G4   G1  #>  "d" "cd" "bc" "bc"  "b"  "a" compact_letter_display(   x1 = dunn$post_hoc$x1,   x2 = dunn$post_hoc$x2,   pvalues = dunn$post_hoc[[padj_name]],   grp_names = summary_tab$GROUP,   centers = summary_tab$MED,   display_letters = as.character(1:6),   display_null_letter = "_" ) #>      G3      G6      G2      G5      G4      G1  #> "___4_" "__34_" "_23__" "_23__" "_2___" "1____" p <- c(0.20, 0.04, 0.008, 0.0005, 1e-6)  pval2asterisk(p) #> [1] "ns"  "*"   "**"  "***" "***" pval2asterisk(p,               break_points = c(0.05, 0.01, 0),               symbols = c("NS", "S", "HS")) #> [1] "NS" "S"  "HS" "HS" "HS"

title: oneway
text: practical way use oneway : Confirm design genuinely one-way: one independent grouping variable one quantitative response variable. Inspect sample sizes, descriptive statistics, possible outliers, distributional shape. Use oneway_anova() parametric omnibus analysis appropriate. Use oneway_art() aligned-rank-transform analysis justified. Use Kruskal_Wallis_test() rank-based omnibus test appropriate. Choose post hoc procedure matches assumptions balance design. Report estimated pairwise differences, confidence intervals, adjusted p-values, effect sizes (significance stars CLDs). Use pairwise_comparison() want formalize decision process automatically. package’s automatic workflow particularly useful analyze many similar one-way experiments want consistent rule selecting analysis protocol.
